sources.title: Gemini API — OpenAI compatibility
facts: The Gemini compatibility API documents image input with a user messages content block of type image_url whose url is a base64 JPEG data URI.
The audio-understanding example uses a user content block of type input_audio with base64 data and format wav at /v1beta/openai/chat/completions.

sources.title: Gemini API — Generating content
facts: models.generateContent accepts multipart contents and includes image and audio input examples; model-specific capabilities are delegated to the model guide.
Part accepts mutually exclusive text, inlineData or fileData; inlineData carries a MIME type and base64 bytes. Blob lists image MIME types and audio/* examples.

sources.title: Gemini API — Image understanding
facts: The image guide lists PNG, JPEG, WebP, HEIC and HEIF MIME types and states Gemini models can understand images.

sources.title: Gemini API — Audio understanding
facts: The audio guide lists WAV, MP3, AIFF, AAC, OGG, FLAC, MPEG, M4A, L16, Opus, ALAW, MULAW and WebM MIME types.
The current narrative examples use Interactions. GenerateContent encoding is therefore sourced separately from its API reference; this matrix does not enable Interactions.

sources.title: Google Cloud — Image understanding
facts: The guide documents image understanding with one or multiple image parts and a GenerateContent call.
Examples document PNG, JPEG and WebP and fileData.fileUri with mimeType. Cloud Storage and public HTTP URLs have distinct access restrictions.

sources.title: Google Cloud — Audio understanding (speech only)
facts: The supported-model table includes all ten Vertex candidates in this inventory and lists speech transcription, translation or summarization as applicable audio understanding tasks.
The shared MIME list is audio/x-aac, audio/flac, audio/mp3, audio/m4a, audio/mpeg, audio/mpga, audio/mp4, audio/ogg, audio/pcm, audio/wav and audio/webm.
A request supports one audio file; REST examples use fileData and GenerateContent. Timestamp examples add generationConfig.audioTimestamp.

sources.title: Google Cloud — Content REST resource
facts: Part accepts inlineData and fileData. Blob is defined for image, audio and video, requiring MIME type and base64 data.
FileData requires a MIME type and a file URI; its schema describes Google Cloud Storage.

sources.title: Gemini GenerateContent video understanding
facts: GenerateContent accepts base64 video bytes in inlineData and uploaded or supported external video references in fileData. MP4 is documented.
The inline example says total request under 20 MB, while its summary table says under 100 MB. Use tiny fixtures below 20 MB and record the discrepancy.
Default static sampling is 1 FPS. videoMetadata supports fps and clipping offsets. Agentic processing is separate and changes response parts; no such mode is enabled here.

sources.title: Gemini OpenAI compatibility - video input review
facts: The page documents image and audio Chat Completions parts but does not define a direct video input content carrier.
Its video section concerns Veo video generation, and the cached_content example does not define direct video input. Native video support is not automatically OpenAI-compatible video support.

sources.title: Vertex video understanding
facts: The supported-model table includes all ten configured Vertex Gemini models, including 3 Flash and 3.1 Pro previews.
Video files can include audio; documented sources include Cloud Storage, eligible public URLs, and inline base64. Source-specific restrictions still apply.
Agentic video processing is restricted to named models and v1beta1; default static GenerateContent does not require it.

sources.title: Vertex Content and VideoMetadata
facts: A Part carries video bytes in inlineData or a reference in fileData. Optional videoMetadata applies to either carrier.
videoMetadata fields are startOffset, endOffset and fps. The documented FPS range is greater than zero and at most 24; default is 1.

protocols.notes: The list records published input MIME types, not proof that each format was tested. Use model-specific capability rows together with this protocol. Inline data needs base64 bytes without a data-URI prefix. Ordinary Interactions remains outside scope. File upload and lifecycle are not exercised by this research.

Image MIME support is combined with the image-understanding guide linked from compatibility documentation. The compatibility example explicitly uses base64 JPEG data URI and input_audio format wav; other audio format names are not inferred from the native API. No audio URL carrier or detail-value support is asserted.

Image formats are the shared documented example subset; exact model pages can document further MIME types. Audio is scoped to speech understanding. Inline data and referenced files are separately documented carriers. Existing Vertex interfaces remain disabled and third-party routing is not official direct verification.
